newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Talks underway to sell Israel's Maritime Bank.
newsitem.headline: Talks underway to sell Israel's Maritime Bank.

text.p: Maritime Bank of Israel said on Monday that its controlling shareholders were negotiating to sell their 37 percent stake in the bank to Carmel Mortgage and Investment Bank Ltd.

"The controlling shareholders in the bank came to the conclusion that the continued expansion of the bank over the years must be accompanied by the union/merger of Maritime Bank to an additional party active in the sector, so that the merged body will carry greater weight in Israeli banking," Maritime said in a statement.

The holding is being sold by a group led by U.S. investor Michael Steinhardt, which acquired Maritime in 1992. The group had hoped to focus Maritime, Israel's smallest commercial bank with a balance sheet of 660 million shekels at the end of September, on capital market activities.
However, the Israeli stock market went into a slump in early 1994.
Maritime managing director David Levinson told Reuters that the talks were in their early stages. "I expect they will be completed within a few weeks," he said.
Sources close to the negotiations said they expected the two banks would be merged.
Carmel received a general commercial banking licence, but it still focuses entirely on home lending.
